subject: maths
title: Chapter 3 · Test 4
summary: Fifteen questions on Pythagoras’ theorem in 2D and 3D, the trigonometric ratios, finding sides and angles, and angles of elevation and depression.
body: This test covers Chapter 3: Pythagoras’ theorem (in 2D and 3D), the trigonometric ratios, finding side lengths and angles with trigonometry, and angles of elevation and depression. It has 15 questions, from easy to challenge. Allow about 25 minutes and work with no notes. You need a scientific calculator for this chapter — set it to degree mode before you start. Diagrams are drawn to scale, but always calculate rather than measure. Sketch and label the right-angled triangle for each question, round only at the end, and give the units.

questions.prompt: How long is the hypotenuse x of this triangle?
questions.explanation: x² = 2.4² + 0.7² = 6.25, so x = 2.5 m. Adding the lengths (3.1) skips the squaring.
steps: x is opposite the right angle, so it is the hypotenuse: x² = 2.4² + 0.7².

mistakes.B: Step 2: you added the lengths. Square each side first, then add.
mistakes.C: Step 3: 6.25 is x². Take the square root.
mistakes.D: Step 2: to find the hypotenuse, add the squares — don’t subtract them.

questions.diagram_alt: A right-angled triangle with shorter sides 2.4 m and 0.7 m and hypotenuse x.

questions.prompt: Write cos θ for the triangle shown, in simplest form.
questions.explanation: cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse = 15/25 = 3/5. 4/5 uses the wrong pair of sides.
steps: Label from θ: opposite = 20, adjacent = 15, hypotenuse = 25.

mistakes.A: Step 2: 4/5 is sin θ (SOH). Cos is CAH.
mistakes.B: Step 2: 4/3 is tan θ (TOA). Cos is CAH.
mistakes.D: Step 3: the fraction is upside down. In CAH, the adjacent goes on top.

questions.diagram_alt: A right-angled triangle with 15 cm next to θ, 20 cm across from θ and hypotenuse 25 cm.

questions.prompt: From a plane, the angle of depression to the start of the runway is 7°. What is the angle of elevation θ from the start of the runway to the plane?
questions.explanation: The horizontal at the plane is parallel to the ground, so the angle of depression and the angle of elevation are equal alternate angles: θ = 7°.
steps: The dashed horizontal at the plane is parallel to the ground.
The line of sight crosses both parallel lines, making alternate (Z) angles.
Alternate angles are equal, so θ = 7°.

mistakes.A: Step 2: you subtracted from 90°. The two angles are alternate angles, so they are equal.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you subtracted from 180°. Alternate angles are equal, not supplementary.
mistakes.D: Step 2: the angles aren’t added. Alternate angles are equal.

questions.diagram_alt: A plane with a dashed horizontal line; the angle of depression from the plane to the runway is 7°, and the angle of elevation from the runway to the plane is θ.

questions.prompt: Find x, the side opposite the 33° angle, correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.explanation: sin 33° = x/20, so x = 20 × sin 33° ≈ 10.89 cm. 36.72 cm comes from doing the opposite operation (x is on top).
steps: Label from the 33° angle: 20 cm is the hypotenuse; x is the opposite.
Hypotenuse and opposite means SOH: sin 33° = x/20.

mistakes.A: Step 3: x is on top in the equation, so multiply — you did the opposite.
mistakes.B: Step 2: you used cos. With the hypotenuse and the opposite, the ratio is sin (SOH).
mistakes.C: Step 2: you used tan. With the hypotenuse and the opposite, the ratio is sin (SOH).

questions.diagram_alt: A right-angled triangle with hypotenuse 20 cm, a 33° angle and the opposite side x.

questions.prompt: A rectangular garden bed is 5 m wide and its diagonal is 13 m. How long is the garden bed (x)?
questions.explanation: x² = 13² − 5² = 144, so x = √144 = 12 m. Adding the squares would make x longer than the hypotenuse.
steps: 13 m is the hypotenuse, so x² = 13² − 5².

mistakes.A: Step 1: 13 m is the hypotenuse, so subtract the squares — don’t add them.
mistakes.B: Step 2: you subtracted the lengths. Square them first.
mistakes.D: Step 3: 144 is x². Take the square root.

questions.diagram_alt: A rectangle 5 m wide with a 13 m diagonal; the length is x.

questions.prompt: A shoebox is 30 cm long, 20 cm wide and 12 cm high. Find the length of its space diagonal d.

mistakes.A: Step 2: you added the lengths. Square each one, add, then square root.
mistakes.B: Step 1: that is only the diagonal across the base. Go up the 12 cm height too.
mistakes.C: Step 3: 1444 is d². Take the square root.

questions.diagram_alt: A shoebox 30 cm long, 20 cm wide and 12 cm high with its base diagonal dashed and its space diagonal d.

questions.prompt: Find θ, the angle between the 4.8 m side and the 6 m side, correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: cos θ = 4.8/6, so θ = cos⁻¹(4.8/6) ≈ 36.9°. 53.1° is the other acute angle, which you get from the wrong ratio or the fraction upside down.
steps: Label from θ: 4.8 is the adjacent and 6 is the hypotenuse.

mistakes.A: Step 2: the 4.8 side is the adjacent, so use cos, not sin. Your answer is the other acute angle.
mistakes.C: Step 2: 6 is the hypotenuse. Tan doesn’t use the hypotenuse — use cos.
mistakes.D: Step 2: tan needs two shorter sides, but 6 is the hypotenuse. Use cos θ = 4.8/6.

questions.diagram_alt: A right-angled triangle with 4.8 m next to θ and hypotenuse 6 m.

questions.prompt: Find x, the side opposite the 71° angle, correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.explanation: tan 71° = x/2.5, so x = 2.5 × tan 71° ≈ 7.26 m. 0.86 m comes from doing the opposite operation (x is on top).
steps: Label from the 71° angle: 2.5 m is the adjacent; x is the opposite.
Adjacent and opposite means TOA: tan 71° = x/2.5.

mistakes.B: Step 3: x is on top in the equation, so multiply — you did the opposite.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you used sin. With the adjacent and the opposite, the ratio is tan (TOA).
mistakes.D: Step 2: you used cos. With the adjacent and the opposite, the ratio is tan (TOA).

questions.diagram_alt: A right-angled triangle with a 71° angle, adjacent side 2.5 m and opposite side x.

questions.prompt: Use a calculator to find cos 15°, correct to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: In degree mode, cos 15° ≈ 0.9659. −0.7597 is what radians mode gives.
steps: Check the calculator shows D or DEG (degree mode).

mistakes.A: Step 2: that is sin 15°. Press the cos key.
mistakes.C: Step 2: that is tan 15°. Press the cos key.
mistakes.D: Step 1: your calculator is in radians mode. Switch to degrees (D or DEG on the screen).

questions.prompt: From the top of a 35 m lighthouse, a boat is 120 m from the base. Find the angle of depression θ from the top to the boat, correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: tan θ = 35/120, so θ = tan⁻¹(35/120) ≈ 16.3°. 73.7° is the other acute angle, which you get from the wrong ratio or the fraction upside down.
steps: Label from θ: 35 is the opposite and 120 is the adjacent.

mistakes.A: Step 2: tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent = 35/120. You used 120/35, which gives the other angle.
mistakes.B: Step 1: 120 is not the hypotenuse — it touches the right angle. Use tan with the two shorter sides.
mistakes.D: Step 2: cos needs the hypotenuse, which isn’t given. Use tan θ = 35/120.

questions.diagram_alt: A 35 m lighthouse with the boat 120 m from its base; the angle of depression θ from the top is marked.

questions.prompt: A vase is a cylinder with a diameter of 12 cm. The longest straight stick that fits inside it is 20 cm. How tall is the vase?
questions.explanation: The stick (20 cm) is the hypotenuse, so h² = 20² − 12² = 400 − 144 = 256 and h = 16 cm.
steps: The longest stick goes across the diameter and up the height; the stick is the hypotenuse.

mistakes.B: Step 1: the stick crosses the whole width, so use the diameter (12 cm), not the radius.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you subtracted the lengths 20 − 12. Square them first.
mistakes.D: Step 3: 256 is h². Take the square root.

questions.diagram_alt: A cylinder with diameter 12 cm and unknown height h, with the longest stick of 20 cm drawn inside.

questions.prompt: A 4.5 m ladder reaches 4.2 m up a wall. Find the angle θ between the ladder and the ground, correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: sin θ = 4.2/4.5, so θ = sin⁻¹(4.2/4.5) ≈ 69.0°. 21.0° is the other acute angle, which you get from the wrong ratio or the fraction upside down.
steps: Label from θ: 4.2 is the opposite and 4.5 is the hypotenuse.

mistakes.A: Step 2: the 4.2 side is the opposite, so use sin, not cos. Your answer is the other acute angle.
mistakes.B: Step 2: 4.5 is the hypotenuse. Tan doesn’t use the hypotenuse — use sin.
mistakes.C: Step 2: tan needs two shorter sides, but 4.5 is the hypotenuse. Use sin θ = 4.2/4.5.

questions.diagram_alt: A 4.5 m ladder leaning against a wall and reaching 4.2 m up it; θ is the angle between the ladder and the ground.

questions.prompt: A ship sails 9 km south, then 12 km west, then another 8 km south. How far is it from its starting point, to 1 decimal place?
questions.explanation: Total south = 9 + 8 = 17 km and west = 12 km, so d = √(17² + 12²) = √433 ≈ 20.8 km.
steps: Total distance south: 9 + 8 = 17 km; total west: 12 km.
South and west are at right angles: d² = 17² + 12² = 289 + 144 = 433.

mistakes.A: Step 3: you added the distances sailed. The straight-line distance uses Pythagoras.
mistakes.C: Step 1: combine both southward legs first (9 + 8 = 17 km), then use Pythagoras once.
mistakes.D: Step 3: 433 is d². Take the square root.

questions.diagram_alt: A ship’s route: 9 km south, 12 km west, then 8 km south, with the straight distance d from start to finish dashed.

questions.prompt: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides of 12 cm with an angle of 40° between them. Find its area, to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: The height splits the 40° angle into two 20° angles: height = 12 cos 20° ≈ 11.276 cm and half the base = 12 sin 20° ≈ 4.104 cm. Area = ½ × 8.208 × 11.276 ≈ 46.3 cm².
steps: Draw the height from the top: it halves the 40° angle (20°) and the base, making two right-angled triangles with hypotenuse 12 cm.
Height = 12 × cos 20° ≈ 11.276 cm; half the base = 12 × sin 20° ≈ 4.104 cm, so the base ≈ 8.208 cm.

mistakes.A: Step 3: area of a triangle is ½ × base × height. You forgot the ½.
mistakes.B: Step 3: the base is twice the half-base. Use base = 2 × 4.104…, then ½ × base × height.
mistakes.C: Step 1: 12 cm is a sloping side, not the height. Find the height with trig first.

questions.diagram_alt: A tall isosceles triangle with two 12 cm sides and a 40° angle between them at the top.

questions.prompt: A 25 m flagpole stands on top of a building. From a point 50 m from the base of the building, the angle of elevation to the top of the building is 40°. Find the angle of elevation to the top of the flagpole, to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: Building height = 50 tan 40° ≈ 41.95 m, so the top of the flagpole is ≈ 66.95 m up, and θ = tan⁻¹(66.95 ÷ 50) ≈ 53.2°.
steps: Building: tan 40° = h/50, so h = 50 × tan 40° ≈ 41.95 m.
Top of flagpole: 41.95 + 25 = 66.95 m above the ground.

mistakes.A: Step 3: you can’t add angles (40° + 26.6°). Use the total height in tan⁻¹(total ÷ 50).
mistakes.B: Step 2: the flagpole starts on top of the building. Add the building’s height to 25 m.
mistakes.D: Step 3: the fraction is upside down: tan θ = total height ÷ 50, not 50 ÷ total height.

questions.diagram_alt: A building with a 25 m flagpole on top, seen from 50 m away: the angle of elevation to the roof is 40°, and a dashed line of sight goes to the top of the flagpole.
